record.title: Unauthenticated GraphQL access to any operation by naming it Signup/SignUp/ValidateCurrentToken
record.description: AuthOperation maps the literal Authorization value 'unauthenticated' to a placeholder unauthed user, then only rejects that user when the client-supplied GraphQL operation name is not in a small public allowlist. The operation name is attacker-chosen and independent of the selection set, so any query or mutation can run anonymously by labelling it 'Signup'. No later directive, field middleware or resolver-wrapper blocks the unauthed user, and many resolvers perform no auth.Checks of their own. The unauthed user is propagated to downstream gRPC services, whose server interceptor accepts it without rejection.
record.root_cause: The public-operation allowlist is keyed on op.Operation.Name (client-controlled label) instead of the actual root fields being executed, and unauthenticated state is otherwise enforced only by per-resolver checks that some resolvers omit.
record.intended_behavior: Only the signup/token-validation root fields should be reachable without a valid identity; all other fields should be rejected for the unauthed user regardless of the operation name chosen by the client.

trace.description: Public GraphQL endpoint; the only auth is AroundOperations(AuthOperation()). No AroundFields/AroundRootFields or schema directives are registered.
Authorization header read from the request, passed to userFromIDToken.
The literal token 'unauthenticated' returns UsrUnauthed() (FirebaseUID FIDUnauthed, ProfileID 0) with no credential check; checkPlatform also returns nil for unauthed users (auth.go:495).

Unauthed users are rejected only if op.Operation.Name is not in publicOperations (auth.go:422: ValidateCurrentToken, SignUp, Signup). The name is client-chosen, so naming any operation 'Signup' passes; the context is then populated with the unauthed user and next(ctx) runs the real selection set (auth.go:410-417).
Downstream gRPC services accept FIDUnauthed from metadata and install UsrUnauthed without rejecting.

Resolver has no auth.Checks; it queries Ledger.Shipments filtered by the attacker-supplied profileID and date and returns a packing list including product, case and location data and shipping addresses (logisticsdocs.go:54+, shipments.go:2597). Ledger.Shipments has no user check (ledger/internal/ops/ops.go:971).

evidence.description: Allowlist check uses op.Operation.Name, the only gate for the unauthed user.
publicOperations list is a set of operation names, not field names.
The string 'unauthenticated' is accepted as a token yielding UsrUnauthed.
AuthOperation is the only registered auth middleware for the API.
UpdateClaims has no auth check; r.updateClaims (graph/claims.go:12) looks up users by arbitrary emails and rewrites Firebase claims via AuthClient.UpdateUsers (auth.go:837).
UploadPop has no auth check and writes a proof-of-payment URL for an arbitrary quoteID via Trader.Set (downstream authorization not verified).
Sibling resolvers such as Shipments (line 2796 area) do call auth.Checks, showing the per-resolver check is the intended control and LogisticsDoc omits it.

conditions.description: The API GraphQL HTTP endpoint is reachable by the attacker (Cloud Run ingress/IAM not visible in source; the endpoint is the client-facing API).
None required: Authorization: unauthenticated plus operationName Signup.

execution.attacker_perspective: Anonymous internet client with no account.
payloads: POST /query with header Authorization: unauthenticated and body {"operationName":"Signup","query":"query Signup { logisticsDoc(logDocType: SELLER_PACKING_LIST, profileID: 1, date: \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\") { info { title } tables { rows { cells } } } }"}
instructions: Send the request with the literal Authorization value 'unauthenticated' and X-Platform header of any value (checkPlatform returns early for unauthed users).
Vary profileID and date to enumerate seller shipment data across tenants.
Optionally issue mutation Signup { updateClaims(userEmails: ["x@y"]) } or uploadPOP the same way.
execution.observed_result: Source-level observation, not a runtime result: the unauthed user passes auth.go:404 because the operation name matches the allowlist, and LogisticsDoc and Ledger.Shipments contain no user check on the path.

remediation.strategy: Enforce the allowlist on the actual root field names (inspect op.Operation.SelectionSet) or use an AroundRootFields/directive that rejects the unauthed user for every field except signUp/validateCurrentToken; also remove the plain 'unauthenticated' sentinel from client-reachable token handling; add auth.Checks to LogisticsDoc, UpdateClaims and UploadPop.

likelihood.reason: Trivial request, no credentials, deterministic; exposure depends only on the API endpoint being internet-reachable, which is unobserved but expected for a client-facing GraphQL API.

impact.reason: Cross-tenant unauthenticated read of shipment/packing-list data including shipping addresses and seller/buyer info, plus unauthenticated invocation of other unchecked mutations (UpdateClaims, UploadPop); full extent across all resolvers not enumerated.

confidence.reason: The gate, its name-based allowlist, the absence of other middleware or directives, and a concrete unchecked resolver with real data were all directly read in source; only network reachability is an unobserved deployment fact.
